cunctim , adv. cunctus,
I.all together, in a body, collectively, for conjunctim (very rare, perh. only in App.): “cunctim et coacervatim (opp.: singulatim ac discretim),” App. Flor. 9, p. 347, 6 ; id. de Deo Socr. 4, p. 43, 39 Hildebr. (al. cuncti).
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
